baseline.detail: The Socket.IO handshake verifies the access token with JWT_ACCESS_SECRET and enforces exp; a refresh token is never accepted (TokenService, AC-001/AC-002).
Room membership is derived from the token's clinic and role; room:join accepts only rooms already owned by the connection (RealtimeGateway, AC-004).
helmet() is applied to the HTTP surface in main.ts before the server listens.
Connection attempts are throttled per IP by ConnectThrottleService in the namespace middleware, with a Redis counter and a local fallback (NFR-013).
Handshake claims and every relayed payload are validated with strict Zod schemas; unknown fields are rejected (AC-012).
No raw Mongo access and no collection exists; the Mongoose connection is the whole Mongo surface (NFR-015).
Payloads are transported as data only; the service constructs no HTML.
Sockets authenticate with a bearer token in the handshake, not an ambient cookie, and the only HTTP routes are idempotent GET health probes. Recorded in spec.md under Security Baseline.
Every variable is read from the environment, validated at boot and never logged; the pino redact list covers token, accessToken, authorization and clinicId.
Helmet's HSTS is enabled; the service sets no cookies, so COOKIE_SECURE has no surface here.

performance.reason: NFR-002 sets a p95 target of 500 ms at 200 concurrent connections, and no load harness exists in the repository to measure it. End-to-end delivery was observed manually during implementation, which is not a benchmark.
performance.method: Not measured. The relay performs no I/O beyond one Redis message and one local emit, which are single-observation timings rather than a p95.

nfr.target: p95 publish-to-delivery <= 500 ms at 200 concurrent connections on one instance
